arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected targeting the Finance OU. The external IP 185.220.101.42 conducted reconnaissance via port scanning on 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), followed by lateral movement and pass-the-hash attacks leading to the compromise of all 23 accounts in the Finance department. Despite detection, automated credential revocation via IAM/PAM was denied due to policy constraints and lack of direct evidence linking individual logins to malicious activity. The endpoint 10.0.10.51 showed anomalous authentication patterns, but user behavior analytics scored risk as low. No malware was found in sandboxed artifacts.

Successful authentication from WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15) to domain controller. Account: CORP\helpdesk.
Multiple failed authentication attempts observed from source 10.0.10.51 targeting Finance OU accounts.
Incident escalated after correlation revealed full compromise of Finance OU via pass-the-hash technique.
Attempt to revoke 23 compromised credentials via T8_iam_pam failed due to policy restrictions and insufficient direct evidence for automated action.

title: Multiple Failed Logins Followed by Success from Same Source
id: 8a9d8f1e-2b3c-4d5e-6f7a-8b9c0d1e2f3a
description: Detects potential pass-the-hash or brute-force attack where multiple failed logins from a single source are followed by a successful login.
status: experimental
author: SOC Team
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    event_id: 4625 # Failed login
  filter:
    logon_type: 3
    failure_code: '0xC000006D' # Unknown username or bad password
  successful_login:
    event_id: 4624 # Successful login
    logon_type: 3
  condition: selection | count by src_ip > 10 | filter by src_ip | within 5m | successful_login
fields:
  - src_ip
  - user_name
  - target_host
level: high

Lateral movement observed from 10.0.2.15 to Finance OU systems. Multiple failed logins followed by successful pass-the-hash authentication.
SIEM correlation identifies anomalous login patterns for j.martinez, s.patel, d.chen across multiple Finance systems outside normal behavior.
Critical finding: All 23 Finance OU accounts compromised via pass-the-hash. Immediate bulk credential revocation recommended.
Attempt to revoke credentials via IAM/PAM (T8) denied due to lack of approval. Repeated attempts also denied.
Attempt to block malicious IP 185.220.101.42 via firewall (T9) denied due to lack of approval.

arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected involving IP address 185.220.101.42. The attacker conducted reconnaissance via an Nmap scan against an internal IT asset (WS-IT-101), then pivoted using compromised credentials to target the Finance OU. Behavioral analysis initially showed low risk, but SIEM correlation revealed 23 failed authentication attempts across multiple Finance users, indicating a pass-the-hash attack. Immediate credential revocation and network isolation were attempted but denied due to lack of pre-approved emergency protocols. All 23 Finance accounts are confirmed compromised.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 performs Nmap SYN scan on WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Detected by IDS as 'ET SCAN Nmap SYN Scan'.
Internal lateral movement observed: successful authentication from WS-IT-101 to domain controller as CORP\helpdesk.
Spike in failed logins from multiple Finance OU accounts (j.martinez, s.patel, d.chen, etc.) originating from internal host 10.0.10.51.
Incident escalated after correlation of UEBA, EDR, and SIEM data confirms pass-the-hash attack.
Attempt to revoke credentials and block source IP failed due to approval requirements in IAM and firewall tools.
